title: Tankers at Sea
abstract: Eight years of tanker traffic, one frame per month — the ships carrying crude oil, refined fuel, chemicals and gas rather than boxes. The pattern is not the cargo map with different colours. The Bosphorus dominates everything, running roughly ninety times heavier with tankers than with cargo ships as Black Sea and Caspian oil squeezes through a strait a few hundred metres wide in places. Rotterdam, Europe's great oil port, burns about three times brighter here than it does for cargo, while Gibraltar and the Dover Strait — which cargo rules — drop back. Brighter means more ship-hours spent in that square kilometre during the month. Built from AIS, the transponder signal every large ship broadcasts, pooled by EMODnet across European waters and the North Atlantic; the rest of the ocean is outside this dataset rather than empty.
